This ensures that dataclasses are always pretty-printed by expanding their fields, even if they have a custom `__repr__` method. This makes the behavior consistent with how `attrs` objects are handled in the same function. The unused `_is_dataclass_repr` helper function was also removed.

The bug was that `rich.pretty` would only expand dataclasses if they used the default dataclass `__repr__`. If a user provided a custom `__repr__`, `rich.pretty` would fall back to using that string instead of pretty-printing the dataclass fields. This was inconsistent with how `attrs` objects were handled, which are always expanded regardless of their `__repr__`.

I have removed the `_is_dataclass_repr` check from the `_traverse` function in `rich/pretty.py` and deleted the now-unused `_is_dataclass_repr` helper function. Now, all dataclasses will be pretty-printed by expanding their fields, providing a consistent and expected experience for users of `rich.pretty`.
